rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING TRI-SERVICE ACADEMIES FOR THE MAJOR SERVICES COMMAND OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
rows.abstract: \"Tri-Service Academies Act\". The bill aims to lessen, if not eradicate, the baneful effects of the 'mistah' system in the Philippine military by establishing separate academies that would shape the men and women who would eventually lead the major services of the military without sacrificing the quality of future officers produced. It proposes the creation of the Philippine Army Military Academy (PAMA), Philippine Air Force Military Academy (PAFMA) and the Philippine Naval Military Academy (PNMA).  The Tri-Service Academies shall provide a two-year officer course that shall embody the academic and training needs of the Major Services Command.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2003-10-06

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE GOVERNMENT ASSET MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Government Asset Management Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Government Asset Management Act of 2003\". The bill seeks to centralize the privatization and disposition of non-performing assets of the government by creating an independent body to be known as the Government Asset Management Authority (GAMA). The GAMA shall primarily handle the privatization and disposition of the non-performing assets of the government. It also provides for the transfer of the management and disposition of surrendered assets from the Presidential Commission on Good Government to the GAMA.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING CHILD PORNOGRAPHY IN CYBERSPACE
rows.abstract: \"Child Protection in Cyberspace Act of 2002\". The measure seeks to address the need to protect our children and the youth from child pornography in the internet. It proposes to impose penalties for the following acts: (a) the act of designing or creating any site on the internet containing child pornography; (b) the act of hosting a site on the internet containing such material; (c) the act of circulating material constituting child pornography through e-mail or through internet chatrooms; (d) possession of an electronic file, whether contained in any form of computer disk or drive, containing material constituting child pornography; and (e) the use of any material, notwithstanding any artistic or aesthetic merit it may contain, for allegedly an educational, scientific or medical purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-10-06

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION ON THE BASIS OF SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND GENDER IDENTITY AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.title_short: The Anti-Discrimination Act
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Discrimination Act\". This bill declares the following discriminatory acts as unlawful: (a) denial of access to public service to any person on the basis of sexual orientation; (b) inclusion of sexual orientation and gender identity in the criteria for hiring, promotion and dismissal of workers, and in the determination of employee compensation, training, incentives, privileges, benefits or allowances; (c) refusal to admit or expel a person from educational institutions on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity; (d) denial of access to or use of establishments, facilities, utilities or services on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity; and (e) other analogous circumstances.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2004-01-19, transmitted to on 2004-01-20 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-21

rows.author: C114
rows.title_full: AN ACT CLARIFYING GOVERNMENT REGULATION AND SELF-REGULATION WITHIN THE COOPERATIVE SECTOR OF COOPERATIVES ENGAGED IN FINANCIAL SERVICES, AND DEFINING THE RESPONSIBILITIES, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF COOPERATIVES AND COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS ENGAGED IN SAVINGS, CREDIT AND OTHER FINANCIAL SERVICES, AMENDING THEREFOR REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6938, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE COOPERATIVE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6939, CREATING THE COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY
rows.abstract: \"Financial Service Cooperative Act\". While the Cooperative Code provides a special chapter on credit cooperatives, its treatment of the financial service operations in this type of cooperative is not substantial. The bill seeks to establish the regulatory framework needed and the financial discipline required of savings and credit cooperatives and financial service cooperatives. It also sets the framework for the amalgamation of savings and credit cooperatives and financial service cooperatives to make them more competitive with major banks and financial institutions. It proposes the creation of the Financial Service Cooperative Commission to undertake the regulation and supervision of savings and credit cooperatives, financial service cooperatives and financial service cooperative federations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2003-10-06

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE POLITICAL PARTY SYSTEM AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: The Political Party Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Political Party Act of 2003\". The bill provides for the institutionalization of national parties and the creation of a state fund for registered national parties. The state fund shall be used exclusively to augment the campaign expenditures and the program operations of the national parties. The bill also defines political turncoatism and sets the prohibition and penalties that will be imposed on elective officials found guilty of political turncoatism.

rows.author: C019
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR INFIDELITY IN THE CUSTODY OF PRISONERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 223 AND 224 IN CHAPTER FIVE, TITLE SEVEN, BOOK II OF ACT NUMBERED THIRTY-EIGHT HUNDRED AND FIFTEEN, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Providing Stiffer Penalties for Infidelity in the Custody of Prisoners
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to increase the penalty for the crime of infidelity in the custody of prisoners by public officers, to with: (a) for the crime of conniving with or consenting to evasion under Art. 223 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC) - prision mayor in its maximum period and perpetual absolute disqualification, without eligibility for parole or probation; and (b) for the crime of escape and evasion through negligence under Art. 224 of the RPC - prision mayor in its minimum period and perpetual absolute disqualification, without eligibility for parole or probation. It proposes to cover all types of prisoners, namely: a) detention prisoners, b) prisoners sentenced by the lower courts, and c) prisoners convicted by final judgment, and punish them with like penalties.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-11-19, transmitted to on 2003-11-20 and received by the Senate on 2003-12-01

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 16 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, MAKING IT MANDATORY FOR ALL COUPLES TO UNDERGO COUNSELLING PRIOR TO THE ISSUANCE OF A MARRIAGE LICENSE
rows.title_short: The Mandatory Marriage Counselling Act
rows.abstract: \"Mandatory Marriage Counselling Act\". This bill provides for a mandatory pre-marriage counseling for all marriage applicants regardless of age. The proposed requirement is aimed at educating couples on the rigors of marriage and how to cope with the challenges they will encounter throughour their married life. The bill also mandates the Department of Social Welfare and Development, in cooperation with the Commission on Population, the Department of Health, the Department of the Interior and Local Government, and representatives of concerned churches and religious sects, to develop a pre-marriage counseling module that will serve as a model for all marriage counseling sessions that will be conducted by government accredited marriage counselors.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENSION OF TEACHERS RETIRED UNDER ACT NO. 3050 AS AMENDED BY PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1148, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Because of the present economic conditions, the pension of teachers who have retired under R.A. 3050, as amended by P.D. 1148 and who have devoted their services in the education sector, is inadequate to defray basic family needs. Retired teachers who are totally dependent of their pension, mostly live below the subsistence level. The bill proposes that the pensions of teachers in the private and public schools be increased by an amount that would decently support them and their dependents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2003-10-06

rows.author: D089
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION OF THE NATIONAL INDEPENDENT COMMISSION AGAINST CORRUPTION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"National Independent Commission Against Corruption Act of 2003\". In the 2002 survey of 102 countries conducted by Transparency International, an international coalition against corruption, the Philippines was reported to be the 11th most corrupt nation. The bill seeks the creation of the National Independent Commission Against Corruption (NICAC) which shall implement and coordinate policies at the national level for the prevention, control and, ultimately, elimination of graft and corrupt practices at all levels of the government, either perpetuated by public officers or private persons.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2003-10-06

The Division shall have the power to compel the execution of an escrow agreement where all payments or reservation deposits made by purchasers before construction is completed shall be held in escrow to guarantee the immediate refund of said amount in case of failure to deliver by the builders and/or developers.

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE SELLING OF FIREARMS, AMMUNITIONS AND EXPLOSIVES, AND SIMILAR OBJECTS, OR ANY PARTS OR COMPONENTS USED IN THE MANUFACTURE OF FIREARMS, AMMUNITION OR EXPLOSIVES TO ENEMIES OF THE STATE AS TREASON
rows.abstract: The selling of firearms, ammunitions, explosives and similar items to enemies of the state is a way of giving aid and comfort to these enemies. It strengthens the enemy in the conduct of war and leads to the possibility of our government being defeated by them. The bill seeks to penalize as treason the selling, directly or indirectly, of any firearms, ammunitions or explosives, and similar items or any parts of components used in the manufacture of firearms, ammunitions or explosives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-10-06

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 45, CHAPTER 10 AND SECTION 17, CHAPTER 1 OF SUBTITLE II, TITLE VIII OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"1987 ADMINISTRATIVE CODE\" BY PROHIBITING A PERSON FROM BEING APPOINTED AS SECRETARY OF NATIONAL DEFENSE WITHIN THREE (3)YEARS AFTER RELIEF FROM ACTIVE DUTY AS COMMISSIONED OFFICER OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: To maintain civilian supremacy over the military, this bill proposes to disqualify all military officers to serve as Executive Head of the Department of National Defense within three years after relief from active duty as a commissioned officer of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP). Three years is deemed to be sufficient time for the relieved members of the AFP to adapt to civilian life.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-10-06

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE ROLL-ON/ROLL-OFF TERMINAL SYSTEM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Strong Republic Nautical Highway Act\". Compared to the usual land and sea routes, the Roll-on/Roll-off Terminal System (RRTS) reduces travel time by 17 hours. Furthermore, the documentary requirement using the RRTS is simplified thereby reducing red tape. This will redound to lower prices of basic commodities and an improved food supply at the local, regional and national levels. This bill seeks to institutionalize the RRTS and consider the same as part of the national highway. Vehicles that can be moved by their own power and passing through such links shall not be burdened by transport procedures and costs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2003-10-06

rows.abstract: The measure proposes to require all foreign or imported theatrical films, including trailers, to be subtitled in the Filipino national language before being allowed for distribution and/or exhibition in local theaters or movie houses. Instead of sending a number of release prints from abroad for distribution in the Philippines, the foreign film distributor may only send a copy of the duped film negative. The duped film negative, through our local film laboratories, can then be printed or duplicated in to several copies for distribution and/or processing and/or printing at the same comparable quality and at equal or lower costs.

The proposed increase in benefits will help boost the morale  of these local officials and motivate them to improve the quality of their work and service to the community.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE VENUE OF THE CRIMINAL AND CIVIL ACTION IN LIBEL CASES AGAINST COMMUNITY JOURNALIST, PUBLICATIONS OR BROADCAST STATIONS
rows.abstract: The prevailing rules on venue of action on libel cases place community journalists and local broadcasters in situations where they have to answer complaints or charged filed, deliberately, in remote or distant places. This may lead to a miscarriage of justice in cases where the accused or defendant fails to appear because of distance and travel constraints. This measure proposes to set the venue for the filing of criminal and civil action in libel cases against community journalists, publications or broadcast stations in the Regional Trial Court of the province or city where the principal office or place of business of said community journalist, publication or broadcast station.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-10-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8436, ENTITLED \"AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMMISSION ON ELECTIONS TO USE AN AUTOMATED ELECTION SYSTEM IN THE MAY 11, 1998 NATIONAL OR LOCAL ELECTIONS AND IN SUBSEQUENT NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTORAL EXERCISES, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES\"
rows.abstract: Considering that there are only 1,991 automated counting machine (ACM) units available for use in the May 2004 national and local elections and considering that there are 192,109 clustered precincts nationwide, prudence dictates that automated counting and canvassing of votes be concentrated in selected and priority areas only. This bill proposes to implement the automated election system in selected and priority areas where there is a heavy concentration of voters taking into consideration the adequacy and security of the ACMs. It further proposes that in areas not covered by the system, the elections for both national and local positions be done manually.
rows.status: Substituted by HJR0032

rows.author: D072
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A REWARD TO ANY PERSON WHO COULD HELP IDENTIFY, LOCATE, PROVIDE INFORMATION, TESTIFY AND PROSECUTE PUBLIC OFFICERS COMMITTING VIOLATIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3019, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-GRAFT AND CORRUPT PRACTICES ACT AND OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENSES COMMITTED BY REASON OF THE FUNCTIONS OF THEIR OFFICE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Informant's Act of 2001\". One of the best ways to fight corruption as well as other forms of injustice is by \"blowing the whistle\" or by exposing wrongdoings so that the public and the government can act on them. While the government offers rewards to informants leading to the capture of hardened criminals, tax evaders and smugglers, there is no operation reward mechanism  that would empower the public to report the corrupt activities of high government officials. This measure proposes a reward system for informants with valid information that would lead to the indictment and/or conviction of corrupt government officials. The reward system proposed in this bill shall be based on the official's salary grade, i.e, the higher the rank of the official , the greater the informant's reward.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-10-08

rows.author: D072
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO DIMINISH PATRONAGE POLITICS BY PROHIBITING SOLICITATION FROM AND THE GIVING OF FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE BY PUBLIC OFFICIALS OUTSIDE OF THEIR OFFICIAL FUNCTIONS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Patronage Politics Act of 2003\". Granting patronage and soliciting special favors outside of official duty corrupts both the populace and the politician. The measure seeks to prohibit solicitations from and the giving of financial assistance by public officials outside of their official functions in order to diminish the system of patronage politics. It proposes to sanction private citizens who solicit unofficial favors from government personnel and heads and also to sanction public officials who give dole outs outside of their mandated duties. The bill distinguishes gifts of nominal value offered as tokens of friendship from items that are expressly prohibited by law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-10-08

rows.author: D031
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING A HIGHER PENALTY FOR THE CRIME OF PERJURY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 183 IN CHAPTER TWO, TITLE FOUR, BOOK II OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Recently, there have been cases where so-called witnesses came out and issued affidavits or statements under oath accusing certain personalities of high profile crimes, only to retract and deny the veracity of their previous statement in the middle of the investigation. The bill seeks to impose a higher penalty upon any person who knowingly issues untruthful statements under oath or false affidavits in the course of an investigation or inquiry in any tribunal other than in a judicial proceeding.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-10-13

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING BARANGAY CAPTAINS OR THEIR DULY AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE/S AUTHORITY TO CONDUCT QUARTERLY INSPECTIONS OF BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENTS WITHIN THEIR JURISDICTION
rows.abstract: \"Barangay Business Inspection Act of 2003\". R.A. 7160 grants local government units, including barangays, the responsibility of protecting its inhabitants from any form of illegal activity. This bill aims to encourage the punong barangay, sangguniang barangay members and members of the lupong tagapamayapa as well as those persons deemed in authority in each barangay, to expose illegal activities such as prostitution and white slavery, the manufacture of illegal drugs, pirated CDs, VCDs, DVDs, clothing apparel and cigarettes, within their jurisdiction. It grants the barangay captain or his duly authorized representative the authority to conduct inspections of business establishments within their territorial jurisdiction.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2003-10-13

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SECURED AND SEPARATE PRISON CELL FOR FEMALE PRISONERS IN EVERY DISTRICT, CITY AND MUNICPAL JAIL, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 63 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975
rows.abstract: National and international human rights organizations and the media have reported several cases of rape and sexual harassment of female prisoners by male prisoners. The measure seeks to provide for secured, clean, safe and sanitary and separate cells for female prisoners in every district, city and municipality jail all over the country. This would safeguard female prisoners from possible crimes or abuses which may be committed while they are in custody.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-10-13

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR HOMEOWNERS' ASSOCIATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for Homeowners' Associations\". Homeowners' associations, in their own little ways, aim to improve the quality of life of their respective members. The bill aims to recognize, support and enhance the role of homeowners' associations in society the nation and the economy. It seeks to remove the ambiguities concerning the role, rights and powers of homeowners' associations by defining and delimiting the same. It also defines the relationship between members and officers of the association, between homeowners' associations and local government units, and between homeowners' associations and concerned government agencies.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE APPOINTMENT OF RETIRED GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, INCLUDING THE MILITARY FOR ANY GOVERNMENT POSITIONS WITHIN FIVE (5) YEARS FROM RETIREMENT
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to prohibit the appointment or designation of retired government officers or officials to any post or government position, including the military, until after the lapse of five years from the date of retirement of the official concerned. Five years is deemed as sufficient time for the retired public official to rid himself of old habits and don a new mantle committed to public service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-10-14

rows.author: D002
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ABOLITION OF JOB ORDER SCHEME OF EMPLOYMENT IN THE GOVERNMENT, INCLUDING GOVERNMENT-OWNED OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS, TOGETHER WITH THE CONTRACTUALIZATION SCHEME OF EMPLOYMENT IN PRIVATE COMPANIES, FIRMS AND CORPORATIONS
rows.abstract: The job order scheme of employment is, basically, temporary in nature and is dependent upon the presence of a job order. Once the job is completed, employment is automatically terminated. This scheme has been abused by local government units and the practice has likewise been adopted by private firms. This bill seeks to abolish the job order scheme of employment in the government, including government-owned or controlled corporations, together with the contractualization scheme of employment in private companies, firms and corporations.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO UPGRADE OF POSITION TITLE AND SALARY GRADE OF STENOGRAPHIC REPORTER II (SG 6) AND STENOGRAPHIC REPORTER III (SG 11) TO STENOGRAPHIC REPORTER IV (SG 14), APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The stenographic reporters in the National Labor Relations Commission (NLRC) perform substantially equal work to those in the judiciary who hold the position of Stenographic Reporter IV (SG 14). Furthermore, the number of cases being handled by the NLRC proper and the Regional Arbitration Branches have risen thereby resulting in the steady increase in the workload of the Commission's stenographic reporters. This bill seeks to upgrade the position title and salary grade of Stenographic Reporter II (SG 6) to Stenographic Reporter III (SG 11) to Stenographic Reporter IV (SG 14).

rows.author: D097
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE USE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS' INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT (IRA), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE \"LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991,\" AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: The local government units (LGUs) are allotted a share in the national internal revenue taxes to ensure that LGUs have the means to support the expenditure responsibilities arising from the devolution mandated under R.A. 7160. This bill seeks to put a stop to the practice of LGUs of using their internal revenue allotment (IRA) as collateral for loans. The practice of using the IRA as a collateral for loans effectively ties up a portion of the IRA. This can result in the delayed payment of salaries and wages and the lack of funds to cover operating expenses.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2003-10-20

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT TRANSFERRING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS AS AN ATTACHED AGENCY AND REDEFINING ITS ORGANIZATION AND PERSONNEL ADMINISTRATION
rows.title_short: Transferring the Philippine Coast Guard to the Department of Transportation and Communications
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to establish the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) as a distinct, armed, uniformed and commissioned service attached to the Department of Transportation and Communications. The transfer is seen to enhance efficiency in the delivery of public service to the maritime sector and spur economic growth in the maritime industry and the coastal areas. It aims to promulgate and develop a coordinated and well-structured maritime program and eliminate fragmentation, overlapping and duplication of maritime safety functions.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06

rows.title_short: Amending RA 7941, the Party-List System Act
rows.abstract: The measure seeks to address the findings of the Supreme Court, in the two cases filed before it, that the existing law (R.A. 7941) is inadequate. It proposes to increase the number of party-list representation in the House of Representatives and to provide a more detailed formula in determining the allocation of seats for the party-list system. It further aims to ensure that the parties elected in the party-list system truly represent the marginalized and underrepresented sectors of our society.

rows.abstract: The measure seeks to prohibit the appointment or designation of resigned elective officials to any position in government or any government-owned or controlled corporation or any of its subsidiaries during the unfinished term of his elective position. The prohibition will discourage elective officials from resigning in order to seek juicy positions in government and strengthen the commitment of elected officials to serve the populace.

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 67 AND 77 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE\"
rows.abstract: The Omnibus Election code sanctions the substitution of candidates who died, are disqualified or have withdrawn their candidacy until noon of election day. This result in confusion among the voters over the abrupt change in the record of candidates. The measure seeks to impose a period within which substitution may be effected. It proposes to require the substitute candidate to file his certificate of candidacy not later than thirty days before the day of the election. The bill also pushes for the automatic relinquishment of office upon filing of this certificate of candidacy of any elective officials, whether national or local, running for any office, including for President or Vice-President, other than the one which he/she is holding in a permanent capacity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2003-10-21

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9164, BY EXTENDING THE TERM OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS INTO FIVE (5) YEARS
rows.abstract: The measure seeks to extend the term of office of barangay officials from three years to five years in order to give these officials more time to implement and effectuate their projects, plans and programs. It further provides for the holding of a synchronized barangay and sangguniang kabataan elections on the last Monday of October 2007 and every five years thereafter.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2003-10-23

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RECOGNIZE AND REWARD THE CONTRIBUTION OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS TO NATION BUILDING, GRANT THEM BENEFITS AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In recognition of the invaluable contribution of Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) or the \"Makabagong Bayaning Pilipino\" to economic growth and nation building, the bill seeks to grant them and their dependents certain rights and privileges. The proposed privileges are in the form of discounts like those enjoyed by senior citizens, and free services. It also proposed to allow private establishments to claim tax credits for the privileges or discounts extended to OFWs and their dependents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-10-21

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE SALE OF MOBILE PHONES AND RELATED TELECOMMUNICATIONS DEVICES, PENALIZING THE REPROGRAMMING THEREOF AND RELATED ACTS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"The Mobile Phone Regulation Act of 2003\". The unregulated use of mobile phones and similar telecommunication devices have contributed to the increase in crimes such as theft, homicide, murder, kidnap for ransom and other crimes. Cases of mobile phone thefts have risen to an alarming level. Likewise, trading in stolen mobile phones has proliferated. The bill aims to regulate the sale, registration, use and re-sale of mobile phones, SIM packs and similar telecommunications gadgets and the reprogramming of mobile phones; and to tackle non-reporting or false reporting of the sale of mobile phones. It provides for penalties for violations of this act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2003-10-21

rows.author: D099
rows.title_full: AN ACT CRIMINALIZING CHEATING AND OTHER DISHONEST ACTS RELATIVE TO THE CONDUCT OF BAR EXAMINATIONS AND IMPOSING STIFF PENALTIES THEREOF
rows.abstract: Time and again, the integrity of the legal profession has been shaken by occurrences and complaints of scandals, cheating and other dishonest acts during bar examinations. These acts have wrought damage to the credibility and integrity of our judicial system and the rule of law. To deter the commission of such dishonest acts, the bill seeks to criminalize cheating and other dishonest acts relative to the conduct of bar examinations. It also provides for the imposition of stiff penalties on offenders of this act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-10-23

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AUTOMATIC ADJUSTMENT OF THE BASIC MONTHLY PENSION OF RETIRED PERSONNEL COVERED BY THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM AND THE SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM TO THE PREVAILING COST OF LIVING INDEX AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: With the buying power of the peso constantly being weakened, the elderly, who depend mostly on their pensions, have difficulty in making both ends meet. This bill seeks to provide for the basic monthly pension and/or benefits of retired personnel covered by the GSIS and the SSS to be automatically adjusted to the prevailing cost of index as determined by the National Economic Development Authority. A pension based on the cost of index would help to alleviate the plight of our senior citizens and enable them to live comfortably in the twilight of their years.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2003-10-23

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING THE IMPORTATION AND DUMPING OF ALL KINDS OF TOXIC WASTES AND MATERIALS INTO THE COUNTRY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Philippines has been tagged as the toxic wastes \"dumping capital\" of the world. Toxic wastes and materials are reportedly shipped and imported continually into the country for either recycling or final disposal. This measures urges the total ban on all kinds and forms of toxic wastes and materials for recycling or for any other use and purpose from entering the country. Likewise, permits issued to any individual or corporation for the importation of toxic wastes and materials, by any government agency, shall be revoked and declared null and void.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2003-10-23

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MANDATORY CLEARANCE FOR ALL GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS UPON THEIR RETIREMENT FROM PUBLIC OFFICE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Honorable Dismissal of Government Officials Act of 2003\". This measure seeks to grant retirement benefits to any government official who retires from public service, pursuant to existing rules and procedures, provided that he/she has no pending criminal, civil or administrative case. It likewise requires the issuance of a certificate of honorable dismissal to all retiring government officials by the Civil Service Commission, Office of the Ombudsman and the Department of Justice, upon the completion of his/her accountability clearance and clearance of no pending case. Any retiring government official without a certificate of honorable dismissal shall be barred from receiving his/her retirement benefits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-10-23

rows.author: C027
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 1801 OF THE TARIFF AND CUSTOMS CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The measure proposes to require all shipping lines, shipping companies, freight forwarders, consolidators, break bulk agents and their agents and sub-agents, and arrastre contractors to state in bold, prominent and comprehensible characters the words \"Customs law requires filing of entry within thirty (30) days from date of discharge of last package from the vessel or cargo is deemed forfeited in favor of the government and shall be disposed of in accordance with law\" in each and every Notice of Arrival sent to the owners, importers, consignees or other interested parties. This shall serve as the \"due notice\" referred to in the Tariff and Customs Code of the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2003-10-23

rows.author: C027
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 52, PARAGRAPH (D) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'REVISED GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE ACT OF 1997'
rows.title_short: Amending Sec. 52, Par. (D) of RA 8291, Otherwise Known as the \"Revised Government Service Insurance Act of 1977'
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to increase the penalty to be imposed upon the concerned officers or personnel of government agencies who fail to remit or causes the delay in the remittance of GSIS payments by more than thirty days from the time the amount becomes due. It proposes the following penalties: (a) increase in the penalty of imprisonment from six months and one day to six years, to imprisonment from ten years and one day to twelve years; (b) increase in the fine of not less than Ph3,000.00 but not more than Ph6,000.00, to a fine of not less than Ph10,000.00 but not more than Ph30,000.00; It retains the present additional penalty of absolute perpetual disqualification from holding public office and from practicing any profession or calling licensed by the government.
rows.status: Business for the day on 2003-11-19

rows.author: D045
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-03, transmitted to on 2004-02-05 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTRUCTURING FURTHER THE MANNER OF COLLECTION OF TAXES ON HORSE RACING AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Tax collecctions on horse racing suffered a major setback when R.A. 7600 was promulgated in 1994. Horse racing afficcionados are discouraged to invest because of the fear that the taxation scheme by be restructured with every change in admission. The measure seeks to stabilize the Philippine racing industry by restructuring the tax scheme on horse racing. It proposes to impose a documentary stamp tax of five centavos on each horse race ticket provided that if the cost of the ticket exceeds one peso, and additional tax of five centavos for every one peso or fraction thereof shall be collected. Furthermore, the bill seeks to levy a 4& tax on winnings or dividends of horse race bettors and a 10% tax on the total prize earned by the owners of winning horses.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06664

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING DISCRIMINATION AGAINST WORK APPLICANTS
rows.abstract: In line with the policy of the State to promote full employment and equal work opportunities, this bill declares as unlawful for any company, agency, institution, industry including hotels, restaurants, and similar establishments to discriminate against any person for employment  because of height , skin, color, physical feature and age. It proposes to penalize any establishment which requires work applicants to meet any physical requirement that are not work related with a fine of not less than Ph50,000 and not more than Ph100,000 for its first offense and for its second offense, the revocation or cancellation of its business permit or license, in addition to the fine.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-10-24
